source.title: When Models Examine Themselves: Vocabulary-Activation Correspondence in Self-Referential Processing

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses the original refusal direction and reports its relation to a separately extracted introspection direction, but it does not test refusal-direction ablation, addition, or weight editing.
record.gate_note: The paper reports cosine similarities between its introspection direction and the known refusal direction, plus a small safety check while steering the introspection direction. It does not intervene on the refusal direction itself. The cited Arditi et al. refusal results are not this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study extracts an introspection direction and reports its cosine similarity to the Arditi et al. refusal direction, plus a 3-prompt refusal check while steering the introspection direction. It never ablates, adds or weight-edits the refusal direction, and never measures refusal rates under refusal-direction interventions. Its results do not bear on any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that a direction distinguishing self-referential processing exists, that it causally steers introspective vocabulary, and that self-report vocabulary tracks activation dynamics only in self-referential contexts. On refusal, they call this direction nearly perpendicular to the refusal direction and say refusal was preserved in a preliminary 3-prompt check. They describe the 'permission gate' as functionally independent of the refusal mechanism.
record.recipe_differences: The study extracts a direction from self-referential versus descriptive contexts using the same token, then adds it at a selected layer to steer introspective output. It does not extract a harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction or ablate that direction.
record.method_sensitivity: The cosine similarity differs by model scale: 0.063 at 70B and -0.026 at 8B.

fits_no_version.finding: The introspection direction is nearly orthogonal to the refusal direction: cosine 0.063 at 70B, -0.026 at 8B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A self-referential-processing direction in Llama 3.1 is distinct from the refusal direction.

fits_no_version.finding: Under introspection steering, 3 of 3 harmful prompts were still refused; the authors call this a preliminary check.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Steering an orthogonal non-refusal direction leaves refusal intact.

record.problems: The refusal-related safety check covers only 3 harmful prompts and is described as preliminary. The paper does not test the refusal direction's causal effect.
record.rows_left_out: Results in Sections 4.3 and 5.2 about near-zero introspective vocabulary on non-self tasks, general task specificity, and the paper's broader introspection findings do not measure the refusal-direction claims.

untested.parts: No ablation or addition of the harmful-minus-harmless direction; no refusal or capability measures under it.
No separation of harmfulness from refusal.
No transfer of the refusal direction.

record.verdict_notes: The record's gate is correct: the study cites Arditi et al. only as a reference direction. It does not say how the refusal direction was computed for Llama 3.1, or at which layer. The refusal check is tiny (N=3).

versions.untested_parts: Does not ablate or add the harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction, or measure its effect on refusal and other abilities.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration evaluation.
No test of attacks suppressing the refusal direction or training against its ablation.
Does not test whether refusal is affine, conical, or mediated by multiple refusal directions.
Does not distinguish harmfulness judgments from refusal decisions.
Does not test transfer of the refusal direction across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct models.
Does not vary refusal training or examine when refusal is trained.
Does not evaluate reasoning models for the refusal-direction claim.
